groups.title: Kitchen and bathrooms
groups.intro: The two rooms people touch every day. Pick the level that matches how you cook and how you like a bathroom to feel.

groups.title: Interior finishes
groups.intro: Floors, walls, doors and light. These set the mood of every room, and they are the easiest place to spend well or spend wisely.

groups.title: Exterior and openings
groups.intro: What the dome wears on the outside, and how it opens to the light. Roofs and windows also carry a lot of the weather protection, so this is worth a careful look.

groups.title: Water and the land around the house
groups.intro: Rain, greywater and the ground outside the door. Skip anything that does not apply to your site.

sections.title: Heating
sections.question: How should the house be heated?
sections.help: A dome holds heat well, so the system can be smaller than you would expect for the size.

good.headline: Electric radiant floor
good.description: Electric heating mats or cables under the floor with a thermostat per room. Simple to install, no boiler.

better.headline: Hydronic radiant floor
better.description: Warm water in PEX loops under the floor, run from a manifold. Even, silent heat and the most comfortable option for bare feet.

best.headline: Infrared radiant panels
best.description: Low-temperature infrared panels that warm people and surfaces rather than the air, zoned room by room.

sections.title: Cooling
sections.question: How should the house stay cool?
sections.help: The same heat pump can heat and cool in the first two levels.

good.headline: Multi-split heat pump
good.description: One outdoor unit and several indoor wall units. Efficient inverter heat pump, room-by-room control.

better.headline: Ducted heat pump
better.description: A ducted reversible heat pump with a concealed air handler, so there are only quiet grilles in the rooms.

best.headline: Passive earth-tube cooling
best.description: Air drawn through buried tubes and pre-cooled by the ground before it enters the house. Almost no running cost.

sections.title: Hot water
sections.question: How should the house make hot water?
sections.help: Solar hot water can be added on top of any of these in the energy step.

good.headline: Small electric tank or tankless
good.description: A small electric storage tank or an electric on-demand heater. Fine for one or two people.

better.headline: Medium electric tank or propane tankless
better.description: A medium electric storage tank, or a propane on-demand heater for endless hot water.

best.headline: Heat-pump water heater
best.description: A high-capacity heat-pump water heater, or a large electric tank. The heat pump uses a fraction of the electricity.

sections.title: Fireplace
sections.question: Do you want a fireplace?
sections.help: For atmosphere, backup heat, or both.

good.headline: Bio-ethanol or electric
good.description: A ventless bio-ethanol flame or an electric fireplace with LED flame and a thermostat. No chimney needed.

better.headline: Wood-burning stove
better.description: A cast iron or steel wood stove with a proper flue. Real fire and real heat.

best.headline: Gas fireplace
best.description: A natural gas or propane fireplace or insert with a real flame at the flick of a switch.

sections.title: Solar panels
sections.question: How much solar do you want on the roof?
sections.help: Sized as an approximate system output. The right size depends on your site and how you answered the electricity question above.

good.headline: About 3 kW
good.description: Around 5 to 7 panels. Covers the daytime basics.

better.headline: About 5 kW
better.description: Around 9 to 11 panels. Covers most of a typical household's use.

best.headline: About 10 kW
best.description: Around 18 to 20 panels. Enough to run heating and cooling on sun, and the starting point for off-grid.

sections.title: Solar hot water
sections.question: Do you want the sun to pre-heat your hot water?
sections.help: Works alongside whichever water heater you chose.

good.headline: Thermosiphon kit
good.description: A simple roof-mounted panel and tank with no pump. Around 200 liters, or about 50 gallons.

better.headline: Pumped system
better.description: A forced-circulation system with a panel on the roof and the tank inside.

best.headline: Multi-panel system
best.description: A larger multi-panel pumped system sized for a big household or for heating support.

sections.title: Battery storage
sections.question: Do you want a home battery?
sections.help: Stores solar for the evening and rides through outages. Required for off-grid.

good.headline: About 5 kWh
good.description: A small LFP battery with a hybrid inverter. Covers an evening's lights and essentials.

better.headline: About 10 kWh
better.description: A mid-size LFP battery. Covers a typical night and most short outages.

best.headline: About 15 kWh
best.description: A large LFP battery. The starting point for off-grid or for running heating and cooling overnight.

sections.title: Kitchen
sections.question: How much kitchen do you want?
sections.help: Cabinets, countertops, sink and faucet, and the appliance package all move together with this choice.

good.headline: Simple and solid
good.description: Clean white cabinets, a laminate countertop, a stainless sink with a chrome faucet, and a straightforward appliance set: oven, cooktop, hood and refrigerator. Everything works, nothing fussy.

better.headline: The everyday upgrade
better.description: Lacquered cabinets with soft-close doors, a quartz or butcher-block countertop, a designer faucet, and a mid-range or energy-efficient appliance package. The kitchen most families land on.

best.headline: Built around cooking
best.description: Premium fitted or solid-wood-front cabinets, a natural stone countertop, an undermount sink with a pull-out faucet, and a pro-grade appliance package. For people who cook a lot and want the room to show it.

sections.title: Bathrooms
sections.question: What level of bathroom fit-out?
sections.help: This level applies to every bathroom you told us about. If you want one showpiece bathroom and simpler ones elsewhere, say so in the notes at the end.

good.headline: Fresh and functional
good.description: Porcelain floor tile, gloss ceramic wall tile, a compact dual-flush toilet, a tub or flat shower pan with a fixed glass screen, a wall-hung vanity and chrome fixtures.

better.headline: Hotel comfortable
better.description: Marble-effect wall tile, a wall-hung toilet with a concealed tank, a thermostatic rain shower on a large anti-slip pan behind a sliding glass enclosure, a soft-close vanity and water-saving faucets.

best.headline: A room to linger in
best.description: Large-format porcelain tile, a designer wall-hung toilet, a freestanding tub, a thermostatic hydromassage shower column in a custom tiled shower, and designer fixtures throughout.

sections.title: Flooring
sections.question: What do you want underfoot?
sections.help: Main living areas and bedrooms. Bathroom floors are covered by the bathroom level.

good.headline: Porcelain tile
good.description: Hard-wearing porcelain tile, plain or in a wood look. Easy to clean, cool in summer, and it lasts.

better.headline: Laminate or engineered oak
better.description: Warm wood look with real oak on top for the engineered option. Comfortable underfoot and forgiving of daily life.

best.headline: Solid wood or polished microcement
best.description: Solid oak, reclaimed wood, or a seamless polished microcement floor. The floors that get commented on.

sections.title: Dome walls, inside
sections.question: How should the inside of the dome shell be finished?
sections.help: The dome shell is concrete. This is the face you see from inside it. The walls between your rooms are a separate question further down.

good.headline: Left as sprayed
good.description: The concrete comes off the spray with a texture of its own, and plenty of people leave it exactly that way and paint straight over it. The rough surface takes the echo out of a room, which is worth more than it sounds. A skim coat sits at this level too if you want it flatter.

better.headline: Troweled smooth
better.description: The crew trowels the concrete smooth by hand while it is still being sprayed. Because it happens on the day, with the material already wet and everyone already up there, it costs less than smoothing it afterward and reads as a properly finished wall.

best.headline: Wood lining or Venetian plaster
best.description: Either oak-veneer paneling fixed over the concrete, which hides it completely and warms the room up, or hand-troweled Venetian plaster with real depth and a soft sheen.

sections.title: Interior paint
sections.question: What kind of paint?
sections.help: All three are washable. The levels differ in how they handle moisture and how the wall breathes.

good.headline: Washable anti-humidity paint
good.description: A washable acrylic paint made for humid rooms. Good coverage, easy to touch up.

better.headline: Anti-mold washable paint
better.description: A dedicated anti-condensation, anti-mold paint for the whole house. Worth it in damp climates and in bathrooms and kitchens.

best.headline: Mineral silicate paint
best.description: A breathable mineral paint that bonds with the plaster and lets moisture pass through. Natural, matte, and very long-lived.

sections.title: Interior doors
sections.question: What should the inside doors feel like?
sections.help: Door leaf, frame and hardware for every room.

good.headline: Lacquered white hollow-core
good.description: Light, clean, white lacquered doors. The standard modern interior door.

better.headline: Oak-veneer solid-core
better.description: Heavier doors with a real oak face. They close with a satisfying thud and block more sound.

best.headline: Solid timber
best.description: Solid wood doors with the weight and grain to match. Built to be refinished for decades.

sections.title: Baseboards and casings
sections.question: What level of trim?
sections.help: Baseboards along the floor and casings around doors.

good.headline: White lacquered MDF
good.description: Crisp white MDF baseboards and casings. Neat and unobtrusive.

better.headline: Solid pine
better.description: Solid pine trim, primed or clear, with a little more presence and a lot more durability.

best.headline: Hardwood
best.description: Oak-veneer or solid hardwood trim, stained or clear, that matches a wood floor and reads as furniture.

sections.title: Interior partition walls
sections.question: How should the walls between your rooms be built?
sections.help: These are the walls that divide the inside of the dome into rooms. Steel framed with plasterboard, which is how Portugal builds them.

good.headline: Standard
good.description: Steel-framed walls with plasterboard on both sides, taped and jointed ready for paint.

better.headline: Sound insulated
better.description: The same wall with mineral wool in the cavity, so bedrooms and bathrooms stay quiet. Worth it on any wall you sleep behind.

best.headline: Sound insulated and moisture resistant
best.description: Moisture-resistant board for bathrooms and kitchens, sound insulation throughout, and a heavier frame for the tall walls that run up into the curve.

sections.title: Lighting
sections.question: How should the house be lit?
sections.help: Built-in fixtures only. Lamps and decorative pieces are yours to add later.

good.headline: LED recessed downlights
good.description: Bright, efficient recessed LED downlights throughout, including damp-rated fixtures where needed.

better.headline: Dimmable downlights
better.description: Dimmable LED downlights, with color-changing options where you want them, so every room can go from work light to evening light.

best.headline: Architectural fixtures
best.description: Feature pendants and architectural fixtures layered over recessed lighting. Light as part of the design, not just the utility.

sections.title: Stairs
sections.question: If there is a second floor or loft, what kind of stair?
sections.help: Only applies if the house has more than one level.

good.headline: Straight softwood stair
good.description: A straight flight in softwood or MDF, painted or carpeted. Simple and sturdy.

better.headline: Hardwood on steel
better.description: Hardwood treads on a fabricated steel stringer. Open, light and solid.

best.headline: Floating cantilever stair
best.description: Wall-mounted floating treads with no visible structure. A sculptural piece in the main room.

sections.title: Exterior finish
sections.question: What should the dome look like from outside?
sections.help: The shell can take render, paint, stone, wood or a stamped concrete pattern. Tell us the look you have in mind in the notes if you have one.

good.headline: Render, paint or basic cladding
good.description: One-coat render or acrylic facade paint, manufactured stone veneer, treated softwood cladding or shingles, or an ashlar-pattern stamped finish.

better.headline: Two-coat render or real wood
better.description: Two-coat spray render or an elastomeric waterproof coating, thermally-modified wood cladding, thin natural stone veneer, or cedar shingles.

best.headline: Stone, composite or textured finishes
best.description: Full-depth natural stone cladding, composite wood cladding, textured acrylic or elastomeric finishes, or premium hand-split shakes.

sections.title: Roofing
sections.question: What should cover the roof?
sections.help: Where the design calls for a visible roof surface over the shell.

good.headline: Asphalt shingles
good.description: Architectural asphalt shingles over an underlayment. The familiar, dependable roof. A rustic thatch option also sits at this level.

better.headline: Cedar shakes
better.description: Hand-laid western red cedar shakes that silver with age and suit the dome's curves.

best.headline: Clay tile
best.description: Interlocking clay tile with the color and weight of a Mediterranean roof. The longest-lived option here.

sections.title: Skylights
sections.question: Do you want skylights, and should they open?
sections.help: Skylights bring daylight into the top of the dome.

good.headline: Fixed skylights
good.description: Fixed glazed skylights or dome cupolas for daylight only.

better.headline: Opening skylights
better.description: Manually opening skylights, small or large, so warm air can vent out of the top of the dome.

best.headline: Motorized skylights
best.description: Electric or solar-powered opening skylights with remote control and rain sensors.

sections.title: Windows
sections.question: What level of window?
sections.help: All levels are double-glazed at minimum with low-E glass.

good.headline: PVC double-glazed
good.description: Tilt-and-turn PVC windows with low-E double glazing. Warm, quiet and low maintenance.

better.headline: Thermal-break aluminum
better.description: Slim aluminum frames with a thermal break, double glazing, and larger sizes available. Argon-filled low-E glass at the top of this level.

best.headline: High-spec aluminum or wood, triple-glazed
best.description: High-performance aluminum with argon low-E glazing, or custom wood and alu-clad wood windows with triple glazing.

sections.title: Exterior doors
sections.question: What should the front door be?
sections.help: Entry and other exterior doors.

good.headline: Insulated steel
good.description: An insulated steel entry door, plain or with a wood look. Secure and weather-tight.

better.headline: Aluminum
better.description: An aluminum entry door, single, with a sidelight, or as a double door, matched to the window frames.

best.headline: Solid wood or custom
best.description: A solid wood or alu-clad custom entry, or a double door with sidelights. The door people remember.

sections.title: Garage door
sections.question: If there is a garage, what kind of door?
sections.help: Only applies if you told us you want a garage.

good.headline: Sectional steel
good.description: A single-skin galvanized steel sectional door.

better.headline: Insulated sectional
better.description: A double-skin insulated sectional door, quieter and warmer.

best.headline: Insulated and motorized
best.description: A 40 mm insulated sectional door with a motor and remote.

sections.title: Shutters
sections.question: Do you want exterior shutters?
sections.help: Shutters give shade, privacy and storm protection. Common in Europe, optional in most of the US.

good.headline: Hinged wood shutters
good.description: Traditional operable wood shutters, a pair per window.

better.headline: Manual roll-down or storm panels
better.description: Manual aluminum roll-down shutters, or removable steel storm panels for hurricane country.

best.headline: Motorized roll-down
best.description: Motorized aluminum roll-down shutters on every window, on a switch or a schedule.

sections.title: Greywater
sections.question: Should the house reuse water from showers and sinks?
sections.help: Greywater is the lightly used water from showers, tubs and bathroom sinks.

good.headline: Diversion to irrigation
good.description: A coarse filter and a diverter that sends shower and sink water to the garden.

better.headline: Treated for toilets and irrigation
better.description: Treatment and storage so greywater can flush toilets as well as water the garden.

best.headline: Whole-house recycling
best.description: Biological or membrane treatment for the highest reuse. The most water-independent option.

sections.title: Rainwater
sections.question: Should the house collect rain?
sections.help: A dome roof sheds a lot of clean water.

good.headline: Above-ground tank
good.description: A tank of roughly 2 to 5 cubic meters, or about 500 to 1300 gallons, with a first-flush diverter, for the garden.

better.headline: Buried cistern
better.description: A buried cistern of around 5 cubic meters, or about 1300 gallons, with filtration and a pump, for toilets, laundry and irrigation.

best.headline: Large cistern or retention basin
best.description: A large buried cistern or a retention basin sized for household supply in a dry climate.

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.question: What should the outside look like on move-in day?
sections.help: Driveway, patio, planting and irrigation. Tell us the approximate area in the notes if you know it.

good.headline: Gravel, slab and lawn
good.description: A compacted gravel driveway, a poured concrete patio, a seeded lawn and a basic drip irrigation kit.

better.headline: Pavers, porcelain and planted beds
better.description: A concrete paver driveway, an outdoor porcelain patio, planted beds with shrubs, and programmable drip irrigation.

best.headline: Natural stone and a designed garden
best.description: A natural stone driveway and patio, a designed garden with trees and planting, and zoned irrigation tied to your rainwater system.
